newsitem.title: FRANCE: French to explain Thomson move to Seoul.
newsitem.headline: French to explain Thomson move to Seoul.

text.p: France's ambassador to Seoul will meet a South Korean government official on Friday to explain a decision to suspend the sale of a Thomson SA unit to Korea's Daewoo Electronics, the foreign ministry said on Thursday.

France on Wednesday shelved a plan to privatise state-owned electronics giant Thomson after an independent government commission objected to part of the sale that would have handed its consumer electronics unit, Thomson Multimedia, to South Korea's Daewoo.
The South Korean government earlier demanded an "understandable explanation" from Paris over the shock decision, which followed French union and opposition protests at the sale to a foreign buyer.
"In the course of his regular contacts with Korean authorities, our ambassador in Seoul will be received tomorrow by the vice prime minister for economic affairs," a foreign ministry spokesman said.
A government source said France would also make clear to Korea that the French government was bound by the privatisation commission's decision.
"We will explain to the Koreans that the government has no authority over the privatisation commission," the source said.

The ministry spokesman said ambassador Dominique Perreau would echo comments by French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis that the privatisation commission's decision did not rule out Daewoo's participation in the privatisation.

"It is not the quality of the companies concerned, not Lagardere nor Daewoo Electronics, that is being questioned. What is being questioned is the terms of the transfer between Thomson and Daewoo," Arthuis said.
The privatisation commission said it could not back the transfer of digital television technology because it was the result of research financed with the help of public funds.
